behavior_constraints: BACKUP <path> flushes the current memtable to disk before copying
BACKUP creates a consistent point-in-time copy of all current SSTable files into the given directory
backup.meta contains a header line `max_seqnum=<N>` where N is the global max seqnum at backup time
backup.meta contains one line per SSTable formatted as `<filename> <level> <max_seqnum>`
BACKUP must not include any WAL segment files in the backup directory
If the backup path already exists, BACKUP overwrites it completely
RESTORE <path> clears the entire current data directory (SSTables, WAL segments, everything)
RESTORE copies the backed-up SSTables into the data directory
RESTORE rebuilds all in-memory state: level assignments, indexes, and bloom filters from copied SSTables
affected_prior: internal/engine/engine.go (rounds 2,3,5: SSTable writers/readers, compaction, memtable flush, indexes/bloom filters must be rebuilt)
internal/mvcc/snapshot.go (rounds 2,6: snapshot state and cursors must be invalidated on RESTORE)
internal/tx/transaction.go (transactions must be invalidated on RESTORE)
internal/mvcc/seqnum.go (round 2: seqnum counter must be resettable to restored max)
internal/wal/wal.go (round 7: WAL segment files must be cleared and re-initialized on RESTORE)
cmd/kvstore/main.go (rounds 2,4,6: command dispatch must add BACKUP/RESTORE commands)
entities.summary: This round adds BACKUP and RESTORE commands that create a consistent point-in-time SSTable-only copy with a backup.meta manifest and restore it by clearing the data directory, copying SSTables back, rebuilding in-memory state, resetting the seqnum counter, and invalidating all open snapshots, transactions, and cursors.

instruction_head: Add online backup and restore. `BACKUP <path>` flushes the current memtable to disk, then creates a consistent point-in-time copy of the database at the given directory path. The backup contains copies of all current SSTable files plus a `backup.meta` file listing each SSTable filename, its level, and the max sequence number at backup time — one line per SSTable as `<filename> <level> <max_seqnum>`, with a header line `max_seqnum=<N>` where N is the global max seqnum. No WAL files in the backup.
